newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: EDP seen surging in first days trade.
newsitem.headline: EDP seen surging in first days trade.

text.p: Shares of state utility EDP-Electricidade de Portugal could rise by up to 20 percent in the first few days after their listing as demand will outstrip supply many times in the privatisation, analysts said.

"If EDP were fixed at 2,000 escudos per share, it could rise by between 15 and 20 percent in the first few sessions, but if the price were set at 2,200 escudos, it would only rise by 10 percent," said one analyst, who asked not to be identified.

Analysts believe that demand will outstrip supply by more than 10 times in the public offer to sell (OPV) component of the privatisation, because applications in the pre-registration period for shares which ends on Wednesday have been very strong.

The analysts said EDP could rise to a "fair value" of about 2,800 escudos per share within a few days of its listing on June 17, a day after the privatisation takes place in a special session on Lisbon bourse.

They said that the privatisation price was likely to be fixed on June 16 at a price at the upper end of the range between the minimum and maximum prices already set by the cabinet between 1,750 and 2,250 escudos.

"EDP will experience strong demand in the 'after market', because the allocation will be heavily oversubscribed. The big institutions will buy on the secondary market," said an analyst, who asked not to be identified.
"2,800 escudos for EDP is fair value," he added.
Another analyst said: "I think that EDP will quickly rise to 2,700 escudos, perhaps on the first day."
The Socialist government of Prime Minister Antonio Guterres is expected to privatise a stake of around 25 percent in Portugal's dominant electricity producer and generator.
If a "green shoe" is implemented, the stake could reach 27.5 percent of EDP's capital of 600 billion escudos.
Under a "green shoe" option, additional shares may be allocated to institutional investors if demand is very heavy.
Analysts said the admission of EDP, which will be the biggest stock in terms of market capitalisation listed on the exchange, should boost liquidity by between 15 and 20 percent.

The local market has already recovered as investors who sold stocks to apply for EDP shares were returning with buy orders after realising that they would not get all the shares that they want in the privatisation, dealers said.
